issues.title: The estimate judge reads plan keys at the top level of the pass --json payload, where the purchase summary is nested under phases[].summary, so the first lookup raises KeyError.
issues.why: fetch_estimate returns json.loads of `pass --estimate-only --json` unchanged; PassResult.to_dict puts each phase's summary under phases[i].summary. _check_scope reads summary["wanted_days"] and the new _estimate_only reads summary["planned_usd"] at top level, so both the full cutover and --estimate crash before judging. Fixed in a7c5e36f (purchase_summary unwraps the purchase phase).

issues.title: judge_estimate buys only on verdict "allowed", but --estimate-only always reports "estimate_only" for a non-empty plan, so the buy step is unreachable.
issues.why: evaluate_spend sets VerdictStatus.ESTIMATE_ONLY whenever estimate_only is passed, and plan_summary emits that as verdict; judge_estimate raises unless verdict == VERDICT_ALLOWED. The verdict line itself predates base, but judge_estimate was rewritten in this diff and the case lists it as B2; a7c5e36f changed the check to estimate_only.

issues.title: --estimate returns BUY and prints the ceiling command for any non-nothing verdict, even when the blocker is something a ceiling cannot fix (archive space).
issues.why: With check_ceilings=False judge_estimate returns BUY right after the nothing_to_buy check. In estimate-only mode the verdict is only ever estimate_only or nothing_to_buy, so a "refused" verdict (sonnet's framing) cannot arrive; the one true case is a space reason appended to reasons, which yields a misleading ceiling command. The real pass still guards space, so this is misleading operator narration, not wrong spending.

issues.title: Over-session names are collected per product, not per volume family, so each family's over failure lists the other family's sessions.
issues.why: _family_evidence keys `named` by product and over_sessions discards each volume check's family; over_failures then attaches all of a product's over names to both its tick-tier and bar rows. Counts stay right but D6 item 4's named listing is wrong data. Fixed in a7c5e36f (keyed by (product, family)). The secondary `.get("volume_checks") or ()` point is needed for docs that carry no volume checks.

issues.title: --slice accepts any non-empty text and that text names the state files and log.
issues.why: _nonempty only strips; the value builds {slice}-cutover-start.txt, -baseline.json and the log name. True, but it is an operator-typed argument on the operator's own host; a mistyped id is operator error, not a defect a reviewer would block on.

issues.title: The configured type checker (mypy, files = src) does not cover the new scripts and tests.
issues.why: [tool.mypy] files = ["src/manta_trading"] and there is no pyright config; pyproject.toml is not changed in base..head. The coverage gap is in existing configuration.

issues.title: A reused baseline is not checked for the records key until evidence collection, after install and purchase.
issues.why: record_start_and_baselines returns an existing baseline as-is and only _baseline_records (in collect) raises "predates 307". Baselines are per slice, so the only way to hit it is re-running with an old slice id's files; an operator-misuse scenario.

issues.title: Exit codes and the complete bucket are defined locally in cutover_304_evidence.py instead of imported.
issues.why: EXIT_OK, EXIT_PARTIAL = 0, 3 and COMPLETE are local while purchase_verdicts imports tick_exit; the EXIT line predates base and values match. Duplication only.

issues.title: Unit-test fixtures use verdicts ("allowed", "refused") the estimate-only producer never emits, and a resubmit branch is untested.
issues.why: test_cutover_304_checks builds summaries with verdict "allowed" and "refused"; real estimate-only output is estimate_only. This is why B2 escaped, but as a finding it is a test-fixture gap, not the defect itself (graded under I2).

issues.title: A wanted family whose caught_up is None (no source edge) passes the D6 item 3 rule with nothing listed.
issues.why: not_caught_up_report returns empty unless caught_up is False. caught_up is None only when no dataset edge is known (family_source_edge/scope_caught_up), and run_gates already refuses a missing dataset edge before any spend, so the case is speculative hardening.

issues.title: Loose type annotations in new code and tests (untyped origins = {}, bare dict/list, -> object, __doc__ used as str).
issues.why: The annotations are as described (first_purchase.py:171, :209; test_purchase_verdicts.py:76, 187, 207, 250, 273-274), but the project's configured checker is mypy over src only, and none of these changes runtime behavior; __doc__ is None only under -OO.

issues.title: EXIT_USAGE is defined and never used.
issues.why: EXIT_USAGE = 2 at line 79 has no reference; main returns argparse's code. Dead constant, removed in a7c5e36f.

issues.title: Session evidence reads only history wants, so the ES and GC tbbo tick-tier families are never judged by the D6 item 3 exit rule.
issues.why: coverage_reads iterates entry.history only, so not_caught_up_report is never called for the tbbo tier, while D6 item 2 lists tbbo and item 3 and the exit criterion require every family not caught up to have each session named. An unhealthy tbbo family with an unchanged health baseline would pass unnamed. Impact is bounded because 307 buys no tbbo days.

issues.title: Every provider_hole session is skipped from the not-caught-up report, though only holes on provider-missing days are exempt.
issues.why: _LISTED_NEVER includes PROVIDER_HOLE unconditionally. classify_day returns PROVIDER_HOLE for a unit whose fetch_status is PROVIDER_HOLE regardless of condition, and tick_status.caught_up exempts a hole only when provider_missing; D6 item 3 says the same. A hole on an available day leaves the family not caught up yet produces no line and no failure, so the exit rule passes silently.

issues.title: --estimate runs the installed production mt, so it prices the old universe's wants, not the requested release's.
issues.why: _estimate_only never installs; fetch_estimate calls `sudo mt-run` (the installed release), and preflight only resolves the ref. Before 307 is installed the universe lacks the widened bars and GC bars, so the D4 ceiling command is derived from the wrong plan. The full cutover still stops on short ceilings before spending and prints the right command, so it costs a re-run, not money.

issues.title: The record-totals baseline is read before install, so it lacks the new GC bar_1m family and totals_delta raises after the purchase.
issues.why: _steps calls record_start_and_baselines (accounting via the installed mt) before install_release. Accounting reports one row per family_wants family, and the base universe gives GC no ohlcv-1m want, so the baseline has no GC/bar_1m; after the purchase totals_delta raises on the missing key. Re-runs reuse the same baseline, so evidence step 5 can never complete.

issues.title: resubmit_origins does not guard against naive requested_at, so comparing with the aware start would raise TypeError.
issues.why: requested_at is TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL, so psycopg yields an aware datetime and _cell's isoformat carries an offset; a naive value cannot arrive from the real CLI. Speculative hardening (the author added the guard anyway in a7c5e36f).

issues.title: Three cutover scripts are slightly over the ~300-line guideline.
issues.why: cutover_304_checks.py is 311 lines and the others are near 308-312. Style guideline only.

issues.title: Session dates and request ranges are compared as ISO strings, and gh state is matched by a string literal.
issues.why: _label compares str(range_start) and str(session_date), which _cell renders as YYYY-MM-DD, so lexicographic order is correct today; unknown buckets already raise CutoverError. Fragility against a hypothetical format change, no current wrong behavior.

issues.title: main catches SystemExit from argparse and converts its code with int().
issues.why: The swallow is narrow and commented; argparse only exits with int codes, so the str-code ValueError is theoretical.

issues.title: No test that --estimate with a resubmit refuses without reading debug requests.
issues.why: judge only reads debug requests when since is not None, and _check_resubmit raises for since None; the path is correct and only a test is missing.

issues.title: The "want has no end date" loop and message are duplicated in coverage_reads and latest_want_end.
issues.why: Both functions walk TICK_UNIVERSE histories and raise the same message; the universe comment already forbids open ends. DRY concern with no behavior impact (sonnet-high/2/0's exit-code half is the same point as I8).
